description: The plot illustrates how three accuracy-related metrics (Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy) vary as a function of Initial Confidence. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.86 to 1.00 with tick labels at about 0.86, 0.88, 0.89, 0.90, 0.91, 0.92, 0.93, 0.94, 0.95, 0.96, 0.97, 0.98, 0.99, and 1.00. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with regularly spaced ticks at 0.2 intervals. The “Final Accuracy” series is a blue solid line with circular markers and vertical error bars; it stays high across the x-range, starting near 0.92 at 0.86 and ending near 0.98 at 1.00, with values around 0.96–1.00 through most mid-to-high confidence points and reaching about 1.00 around 0.98–0.99. The “Δ Accuracy” series is an orange dashed line with diamond markers and vertical error bars; it begins around 0.28 at 0.86, declines to roughly 0.12–0.15 around 0.90–0.91, rises to about 0.20 at 0.92, then drops to its lowest region near 0.05–0.07 around 0.94–0.96, and finishes higher near 0.20 at 1.00. The “Initial Accuracy” series is a green dash-dot line with square markers and vertical error bars; it starts around 0.64 at 0.86, increases through about 0.75–0.84 by 0.89–0.91, dips near 0.77 at 0.92, rises to around 0.90–0.92 by 0.94–0.96, stays near 0.88–0.91 through about 0.97–0.99, and then drops to roughly 0.76 at 1.00.
